FOR SEAN[image]Day Two and Graduation Day at the K9 Sergeant Sean M. Gannon Training Center in Yarmouth. What a great day to be back at the house that Sean built.[image][image]After two days of intense, hands-on training, we celebrated the graduation of an incredible group of police officers who stepped up to learn and sharpen their skills as K9 decoys. This training is so important to building safe, effective K9 teams and preparing these officers and dogs for the challenges they face protecting our communities.[image][image]Congratulations to our graduating officers:[image][image]Sean Lowe — Falmouth Police Department[image]Kevin Lynch — Cohasset Police Department[image]Brandon Sanders — Barnstable Police Department[image]Dan Ruth — Barnstable Police Department[image]Richard Proctor — Plymouth County Sheriff’s Office[image]Glenn Haley — Plymouth County Sheriff’s Office[image]Joe Silva — Plymouth County Sheriff’s Office[image]Bryan Lobianco — Hingham Police Department[image]Andrew Latosek — Medway Police Department[image]Liam Breen — Yarmouth Police Department[image]Bryan Derochea — Mashpee Police Department[image]Brian Smith — West Bridgewater Police Department[image][image]Thank you to the instructors, the participating departments, and everyone who made these two days of training and today’s graduation possible. The dedication of these officers is impressive, and these K9s are absolutely amazing.[image][image]Our family is proud to help make this training possible through a $5,000 grant from Big Nick’s Ride and the Nicholas G. Xiarhos Memorial Fund, in memory of our son Nick and in memory of the son of our good friends Denise and Patrick Gannon.[image][image]Sean dreamed of building a place where K9 teams could train and become better prepared to protect others. Seeing that dream continue to make a difference, and knowing that Nick’s legacy is helping support these officers, means more than words can say.[image][image]Congratulations to all 12 graduates. Thank you for your commitment to serving and protecting others.[image][image]We will always Back the Blue. We will continue doing everything we can to support our police officers and K9 teams with the training and equipment they need to do their jobs safely and effectively.[image][image]Pain to purpose. GOOD MORNING & HAPPY THANKFUL THURSDAY [image]Operation Flags for Vets[image][image]Today we are especially thankful for the Monti family and the incredible tradition they continue to carry on in honor of their son and brother, U.S. Army Sergeant Jared C. Monti—a Medal of Honor recipient—our nations highest honor. [image][image]Jared was born and raised right here in Massachusetts and gave his life serving our country in Afghanistan. His incredibly strong and proud father, Paul Monti, turned his unimaginable loss into a lasting mission of love, remembrance and service.[image][image]That mission became Operation Flags for Vets.[image][image]Twice a year, during Veterans Day week and Memorial Day week, volunteers gather at our Massachusetts National Cemetery in Bourne to place American flags on the graves of our fallen heroes.[image][image]People come from all over. Young and old. Veterans, families, friends and complete strangers. They walk among the graves, place a flag, and say the name of the hero who rests there.[image][image]That is what makes this tradition so powerful.[image][image]It reminds us that these men and women are not forgotten.[image][image]As the years have gone by, the tradition continues. The Monti family continues to lead, and thousands of people continue to show up to honor Jared and every hero who made the ultimate sacrifice for our country.[image][image]Flag Placement Day is November 7th at 9:00 AM.[image]Flag Pickup Day is November 14th at 9:00 AM.[image][image]We hope to see you there.[image][image]God bless the Monti Gold Star family, every Gold Star family who carries this loss every single day, and all those who have served, all those who continue to serve, and every volunteer who takes the time to place and retrieve these flags.[image][image]Happy Thankful Thursday, Cape Cod. [image][image]See you on November 7th and 14th. GOOD MORNING AND HAPPY REMEMBER EVERYONE DEPLOYED FRIDAY![image][image]FROM TRAGEDY TO TRIUMPH![image][image]Some GREAT NEWS to share![image][image]My good friend James LaMonte and his team at the K9 PTSD Center in Seekonk continue to do incredible work for our four-legged heroes.[image][image]The new Massachusetts K9 license plates are arriving! Thousands have been ordered, and you’ll be seeing them all over the Commonwealth.[image][image]The plates feature K9 Nero, a Belgian Malinois, with the letters SG honoring Sergeant Sean Gannon. They also recognize K9 Mikey, a retired Boston Police K9 German Shepherd who was James LaMonte’s first dog.[image][image]The money raised helps support the dogs at the Seekonk center and the planned second Canine PTSD Center right here in Bourne on Cape Cod![image][image]And don’t forget, we hold an annual blood drive for dogs in Sean’s memory. Best of all, Nero is still alive and STILL RUNNING STRONG![image][image]Please join us October 18th in Bourne for the first-ever K9 5K on Cape Cod! We’ll recognize the incredible K9 heroes and their handlers from across the Commonwealth, and we hope to make it an annual tradition.[image][image]Think about how far we’ve come since the tragic loss of Sean Gannon and the shooting of his devoted partner, Nero.[image][image]We’ve built the K9 Sergeant Sean M. Gannon Training Center at Yarmouth Police Headquarters, Sean’s dream. We’ve passed Nero’s Law and Dakota’s Law, established a nonprofit in Sean’s memory, organized an annual K9 blood drive, and now have these new license plates. And there’s so much more to come![image][image]Sometimes, when horrible things happen, we look for a reason why. Sometimes, we have to turn that tragedy into something that helps others and makes a difference. And that’s exactly what we’re doing.[image][image]I think about Sean’s parents, Denise and Patrick, his wife Dara, his siblings, and all their family and friends. Can you imagine what it must mean to see all the good that has come from Sean’s life and sacrifice?[image][image]From saving dogs to training officers, these four-legged heroes serve alongside our military, police, and corrections officers. Dogs like Nero, Thor, Dakota, Kitt, Frankie, and so many others deserve our support.[image][image]Sean’s legacy lives on. And it doesn’t stop here. It never will.[image][image]Remember Everyone Deployed. Give your dog an extra treat, and keep an eye out for the new K9 license plates on vehicles all over the Commonwealth![image]🇺🇸💙🐕👏🏻[image]#RepX #Fightin5th #ProudAmerican #ServiceBeforeSelf #K9 #BackTheBlue #NerosLaw #DakotasLaw #CapeCod #Massachusetts #MAPolice #ForSean[image]K9 PTSD Center[image]Healing Dakota[image]Rehoboth K9 Edo[image]Barnstable Police K9 Foundation[image]K9 Flexx and Retired/Police K9 Mr. Warner.[image]K9 Kitt Foundation[image]K9 Hurricane's Heroes[image]The Plymouth County Sheriff's Department[image]Riptide K-9[image]State Representative Justin Thurber[image]Senator Kelly Dooner[image]Cape Cod Realtor Lori Jurkowski[image]Support Our Troops - Wear Red Friday's[image]Modern Primitive K9[image]Denise Morency Gannon

[image]HAPPY SATURDAY![image][image]REP X YARD SIGNS![image][image]With Election Day coming up on November 3rd, we’re checking in with friends and neighbors across the Fightin’ Fifth![image][image]If you’d like a Rep X yard sign for your home or business, just send us a message with your town and let us know. We’d be happy to get one to you![image][image]Thank you for your continued support, friendship, and confidence over the years. It’s an honor to serve our communities, and I never take that responsibility for granted.[image][image]THANK YOU for being part of the GREAT FIGHTIN’ FIFTH! HOUSEHOLD HAZARDOUS WASTE COLLECTION TODAY IN BARNSTABLE [image][image]Happy to stop by again this morning at the Barnstable Household Hazardous Waste Collection at the Barnstable Transfer Station in Marstons Mills, happening today from 9 AM to 12 PM.[image][image]This is a GREAT service for our residents and an important way to safely dispose of paints, chemicals, cleaners, and other materials that should NEVER go in our regular trash or down the drain.[image][image]A BIG THANK YOU to everyone who helped organize today’s collection and to all the residents doing their part to dispose of these materials safely and responsibly.[image][image]Protecting our environment, our drinking water, and the beautiful Cape Cod we all love is something we can ALL do our part to support.[image][image]GREAT JOB, TOWN OF BARNSTABLE AND BARNSTABLE COUNTY![image][image]KEEP CAPE COD CLEAN.
